2608.24534.title: Neurosymbolic Alignment for Physiologically-Safe Clinical Language Models
2608.24534.paper_summary: Clinical LLMs can generate recommendations that are factually plausible yet physiologically unsafe. We investigate whether safety alignment can be improved by grounding preference optimization in structured physiological knowledge rather than text-only supervision. Methods: We propose Neurosymbolic Alignment, a training-time framework that couples a 7B clinical LLM with an HGNN-based Physiological World Model over an 847K-node biomedical knowledge graph. Candidate responses are scored using homeostatic constraints, multi-hop path plausibility, and drug-interaction penalties, and the resulting rankings drive iterative on-policy ORPO updates. Evaluation is performed on the Clinical Safety Benchmark (CSB), a 2,500-scenario benchmark for physiological constraint violations in generative clinical reasoning. Results: Relative to ORPO, the proposed method improves CSS from 69.5% to 90.8% (+21.3 pp), reduces physician-evaluated HR from 14.1% to 5.1% on the blinded subset, and improves DID from 72.8% to 91.6%. These gains are corroborated by an HGNN-independent Rule-Engine Safety Score (RSS: 86.4%, +21.2 pp over ORPO; r=0.97 concordance with CSS). The method also exceeds GPT-4 (5-shot) on all safety metrics despite a 10x parameter disadvantage, and outperforms an inference-time self-correction pipeline (SFT+SelfCorrect) by 11.4 pp CSS. Under synthetic EHR-style noise, 84.2% CSS is retained. Ablation analysis shows that HGNN scoring (-16.2 pp) and iterative training (-11.5 pp) are the dominant contributors. PhysioScore calibration against 200 clinician labels yielded ECE = 0.038 and kappa = 0.91. Conclusion: Training-time physiological grounding produces measurable and independently verifiable safety improvements in open-weight clinical LLMs under controlled evaluation. External validation on real clinical data is required to determine whether these gains transfer to deployment settings
2608.24534.paper_summary_zh: 臨床 LLM 可以生成事實上合理但生理上不安全的建議。我們研究是否可以通過將偏好優化基於結構化生理知識而非僅依賴文本監督來改善安全對齊。方法：我們提出了神經符號對齊，這是一種訓練時框架，將一個 7B 的臨床 LLM 與基於 HGNN 的生理世界模型結合在一個擁有 847K 節點的生物醫學知識圖譜上。候選響應使用穩態約束、多跳路徑合理性和藥物相互作用懲罰進行評分，並且結果排名推動迭代的政策內 ORPO 更新。評估是在臨床安全基準 (CSB) 上進行的，這是一個針對生成臨床推理中生理約束違規的 2,500 情境基準。結果：相對於 ORPO，所提出的方法將 CSS 從 69.5% 提高至 90.8% (+21.3 pp)，在盲測子集中將醫生評估的 HR 從 14.1% 降低至 5.1%，並將 DID 從 72.8% 提高至 91.6%。這些增益得到了 HGNN 獨立的規則引擎安全分數 (RSS: 86.4%，比 ORPO 增加 21.2 pp；r=0.97 與 CSS 的一致性)。該方法在所有安全指標上超過了 GPT-4 (5-shot)，儘管存在 10 倍的參數劣勢，並且在推理時自我修正管道 (SFT+SelfCorrect) 上超出 11.4 pp CSS。在合成 EHR 風格噪聲下，保留了 84.2% CSS。消融分析顯示，HGNN 評分 (-16.2 pp) 和迭代訓練 (-11.5 pp) 是主要貢獻者。對 200 名臨床醫生標籤的 PhysioScore 校準產生了 ECE = 0.038 和 kappa = 0.91。結論：訓練時的生理基礎在受控評估下產生可測量且獨立可驗證的安全改進，適用於開放權重的臨床 LLM。需要對真實臨床數據進行外部驗證，以確定這些增益是否能轉移到部署環境中。
